title: Variant call rate

blocks.what_we_do: We remove variants with a call rate below 98%. We do this after sample [quality control](docs/glossary.md#quality-control) (QC), which already removed the poor samples in module 3.
blocks.why:
A call is the result for one variant in one sample. A failed call is called missing data, or [missingness](docs/glossary.md#missingness). The call rate of a variant is the share of samples where the call worked.

In module 3 we checked each sample. Now we check each variant in the samples that remain. A [probe](docs/glossary.md#probe) is the small piece of DNA on the chip that measures one variant. A probe can work badly in many wells, even when every sample passes sample QC. A well is one small hole on the plate that holds one sample.

The number of failing variants can be higher than the number of failures planted on purpose. The simulation planted 800 low-call variants. Natural patterns in the [genotypes](docs/glossary.md#genotype) also cause some failures. The earlier removals also change which samples are counted.
blocks.you_need: The full dataset saved at the end of sample QC. This saved point is called a [checkpoint](docs/glossary.md#checkpoint). Here it is boundary 3.8, made in step 3.8.
blocks.command:
Copy the R chunk into the R console (the window where you type R commands) and press Enter. R then runs the PLINK 2 program for you.

```{r s4-1}
# 1. Remove variants with more than 2% of their results missing.
run_plink(cfg, c("--pfile", guided_path(cfg, "3.8"), "--geno", "0.02", "--make-pgen", "--out", guided_path(cfg, "4.1")))
# Course bookkeeping: records the counts for the next step. Do not change.
ops <- guided_replay_lists(cfg, "4.1", "3.8")
guided_register(cfg, "4.1", "3.8", 1844, 295559, operations = ops)
```

Plain PLINK 2 command (use `bin\plink2.exe` on Windows):

```sh
bin/plink2 --pfile results/guided/s3-8_state --geno 0.02 --make-pgen --out results/guided/s4-1_state --threads 2 --memory 2048
```

This is the same command written for a terminal, a window where you type commands. Here is what each option does.

`--geno 0.02` removes variants with more than 2% missing calls in the remaining samples.

`--pfile` selects the PLINK 2 input files.

`--make-pgen` writes a new copy of the data in PLINK 2 format.

`--out` sets the start of the names of the new files.

`--threads 2` limits PLINK to two worker threads, which are parts of the computer that work in parallel.

`--memory 2048` sets the memory PLINK may use, in MiB (a unit of computer memory).
blocks.expected_result:
801 variants are removed. This is not exactly the 800 planted low-call variants. 1,844 samples and 295,559 variants remain.


The tested PLINK version is defined in `config.R` and recorded in
`software_versions.txt`. Validation: executable chunks and the expected counts passed on Windows.
blocks.troubleshooting: Stop at the first error. Check the input file named in the error message, and check the previous step. Keep your command and the console messages. Do not use files from a different version of the dataset. See [troubleshooting](docs/troubleshooting.md).
blocks.what_this_check_can_reveal: It can reveal poor probes, problems in the software that assigns genotypes (called cluster calling) and failures that depend on the sample. Look at which samples are affected. Do not assume that every rejected variant has the same cause.
blocks.quick_check:
Why can a simulation with 800 planted failures give 801 removed variants?

<details><summary>Show the answer</summary>

The rule works on the observed data, including other variants. Its result does not have to match the planted list.

</details>
blocks.files_created: `s4-1_state.*`, the lists of excluded IDs and the records that let the course repeat this step.
blocks.try_other_thresholds:
This optional box is not part of the main path and does not change your results. The examples use simulated data, so the true answer is known ([why](lessons/module_05_population_structure.Rmd#step-5-1)).

Each trial starts from the cohort saved at 3.8 and changes the limit only.

**Chart: --geno.**

**Why this simulation.** Variants with many missing calls give weak data. How strict should the variant filter be?

**How to read the chart.** Each point is one `--geno` value: variants with more than that share of missing calls are removed. The vertical axis counts the variants removed, and the diamond is the course value.

**Try this.**

- Move the slider to **0.2**. No variant is removed, because step 3.1 already removed the worst.
- Move it to **0.01**. Many more variants are removed.

**What you should see, and why.** Step 3.1 already removed the variants with the most missing calls, so looser limits remove nothing. Stricter limits remove variants with a little missing data.

**Why it matters for your GWAS.** [step 4.1](lessons/module_04_variant_quality_control.Rmd#step-4-1) cleans variants after the sample checks. Missing calls that depend on disease status can create false associations ([step 4.2](lessons/module_04_variant_quality_control.Rmd#step-4-2)).

**Key idea:** A variant filter trades the number of variants against the completeness of each.

```{r s4-1_thresholds, eval=FALSE}
# Course check. This step needs project version 2026.5 or later.
if (!exists("requires_course_version")) stop("This step needs project version 2026.5 or later. Your project is older. Download the new version at step 0.3.", call. = FALSE)
requires_course_version("2026.5")
# Optional. Each trial starts from the same input and changes one threshold only.
thresholds <- c(0.01, 0.02, 0.05, 0.10, 0.20)
trial <- threshold_counts(cfg, guided_path(cfg, "3.8"), "--geno", thresholds)
trial$course_value <- trial$threshold == 0.02
trial
# Plot the removed variants. The course value is the large diamond.
plot_threshold_trials(trial, "Variants removed")
# Optional: add engine = "ggplot2" to plot_threshold_trials() to draw the plot with ggplot2 (install.packages("ggplot2") once first).
```
Plain PLINK 2 command for one trial. It writes only small files with the name that you give to `--out`, never a new dataset:

```sh
bin/plink2 --pfile results/guided/s3-8_state --geno 0.05 --make-just-pvar --out results/trials/s4-1_trial --threads 2 --memory 2048
```

The log file `results/trials/s4-1_trial.log` states how many variants were removed. To repeat the trial, change the number after `--geno` and use a new `--out` name.

The expected result of the trials:

| Threshold | Variants removed | Variants remaining |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0.01 | 1,052 | 295,308 |
| **0.02 (course value)** | 801 | 295,559 |
| 0.05 | 560 | 295,800 |
| 0.1 | 0 | 296,360 |
| 0.2 | 0 | 296,360 |
